dedupe_keys.name: national pipeline mapping system npms us gas transmission and hazardous liquid pipelines lng plants and breakout tanks

description: The National Pipeline Mapping System (NPMS) is the US Department of Transportation PHMSA data set of locations of and information about gas transmission and hazardous liquid pipelines, liquefied natural gas plants and breakout tanks under PHMSA jurisdiction. Pipeline operators submit their data each year, gas pipelines between 1 January and 15 March and liquid pipelines between 1 January and 15 June, reflecting assets as of 31 December of the previous year, together with the confidence of their location information. The public can use the Public Map Viewer to see pipelines, LNG plants, breakout tanks and accidents and incidents in a chosen county or federal waters, and a tool to find operator contacts by state, county or ZIP code. Government officials and pipeline operators with NPMS accounts and multi-factor login use PIMMA, which shows more scope and detail. Coverage is the United States, excluding distribution and gas gathering lines. The viewer is accessible in a browser at no cost, while GIS data go only to qualifying accounts or through a formal data request. Caveats: PHMSA states the minimum positional accuracy is plus or minus 500 feet, the viewer blanks data at scales finer than about 1:24,000, and it must not replace calling 811. Simulation uses are exposure of oil and gas transmission lines to floods, earthquakes and landslides and emergency planning around pipelines. Related records: data-pipeline-grid-cyber-physical-incident-panel uses PHMSA incident records.
